entries.claim: Historical English source expression: “As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.” This supplies the corresponding English expression at the addressed scope. The cited occurrence is the Ordinary’s Psalm42doxology, not the Magnificat.

The printed first doxology clause supplies the inherited structure with Holy Ghost; this rendering uses Holy Spirit for Spiritui Sancto. The same first clause is reused from Gloria Patri. The cited page prints it in the Mass prayers rather than the Magnificat.
entries.reader_note: This page prints “Holy Ghost”; the formula shown here uses “Holy Spirit”.

entries.claim: As He spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.

Historical English wording basis for both clauses of this verse, including the conceit of their heart. The print has shewn, in his arm and hath; the selected text has shown, with His arm and has, with divine capitalization and punctuation adjustments. The complete verse is revised rather than verbatim.

Historical English wording basis for the complete putting-down and exalting clauses. The selected text modernizes hath to has and capitalizes divine pronouns. The complete verse is revised rather than verbatim.
